chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about a man performing Tamattu' who forgot to shorten (his hair and nails) until he entered the state of Ihram for Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should seek forgiveness from Allah.'

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered the state of Ihram, the sacred state of pilgrimage.
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu', a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between.
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten (hair) or trim (nails), a ritual act required upon entering Ihram.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shorten their hair before entering Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the omission of the *Qasr* (shortening of hair and nails) ritual before entering Ihram for Hajj, when done out of forgetfulness, does not invalidate the pilgrimage but requires only *Istighfar* (seeking forgiveness). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of leniency in minor ritual omissions during the sacred state, distinguishing between intentional neglect and accidental oversight. It underscores the spiritual emphasis on repentance over punitive measures in the context of *Tamattu'*.
